ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the diagram, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, $AB=5\,cm$, $BC=13\,cm$, point $D$ is on line segment $AC$, and $CD=7\,cm$. A moving point $P$ starts from point $E$, which is $15\,cm$ away from point $B$, and moves in the direction of the ray $EA$ at a speed of $2\,cm$ per second, for a time of $t$ seconds. Find the length of $AD$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the Pythagorean theorem, we have $AC=\sqrt{BC^{2}-AB^{2}}=\sqrt{13^{2}-5^{2}}=12\,(\text{cm})$,\\
$\therefore AD=AC-CD=5$,\\
$\therefore$ the length of $AD$ is $\boxed{5}\,\text{cm}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows A, B, P, and E on the same horizontal baseline. Segment AC is vertical, and a right-angle square at A indicates AC is perpendicular to AB, so angle BAC is 90°. Point D is marked on segment AC between A and C. The diagram also includes slanted segments involving C, B, P, and D, but the requested length AD depends on triangle ABC and the position of D on AC. Reasoning: From the given data, AB = 5 cm, BC = 13 cm, CD = 7 cm, and triangle ABC is right-angled at A. The moving point P information is irrelevant for finding the fixed segment AD. In right triangle ABC, BC is the hypotenuse, so by the Pythagorean theorem: AC^2 + AB^2 = BC^2. Thus AC = sqrt(13^2 - 5^2) = sqrt(169 - 25) = sqrt(144) = 12 cm. Since D lies on AC and CD = 7 cm, AD = AC - CD = 12 - 7 = 5 cm.
